assertions.speaker: TACITUS research assistant
assertions.subject: NYC heat resilience: reaching risk beyond emergency days
assertions.proposition: NYC Health reported an annual warm-season average of approximately 500 heat-related deaths, predominantly heat-exacerbated deaths. About 80% occurred on frequent hot days below the extreme-heat range, described as 82–94°F.
conditions: Population estimates, not individually certified heat deaths or a forecast for one summer. The larger aggregate burden on non-extreme hot days reflects their frequency; risk rises with temperature and extreme days are not safer. Outdoor temperature bands are not heat-index alert thresholds.

evidence.evidence/f27992dfffa678fff2ad78955d9c5ce:
NYC Health reported an annual warm-season average of approximately 500 heat-related deaths, predominantly heat-exacerbated deaths. About 80% occurred on frequent hot days below the extreme-heat range, described as 82–94°F.
Qualification: Population estimates, not individually certified heat deaths or a forecast for one summer. The larger aggregate burden on non-extreme hot days reflects their frequency; risk rises with temperature and extreme days are not safer. Outdoor temperature bands are not heat-index alert thresholds.
Primary sources: https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/about/press/pr2026/nyc-health-department-releases-report-on-heat-related-deaths.page
evidence.evidence/5f2a91d915f0bce70e37917b8637598:
The 2026 report changes heat-exacerbated mortality estimation from five-year to ten-year rolling windows; the reported heat-exacerbated estimates cover 2014–2023.
Qualification: Methodological change limits direct comparison with prior editions. The separate direct heat-stress series covers 2016–2025, with recent data provisional; these are not one 2026 cohort.
Primary sources: https://a816-dohbesp.nyc.gov/IndicatorPublic/data-features/heat-report/
evidence.evidence/0f0aba97ecaa77bbdec1957dbdb1f79:
The Heat Vulnerability Index combines environmental and social factors to compare neighborhood heat vulnerability.
Qualification: A relative neighborhood measure, not an assessment of an individual’s health or eligibility.
Primary sources: https://a816-dohbesp.nyc.gov/IndicatorPublic/data-features/heat-report/
evidence.evidence/018cbfa8edac803a9a9ba57bf03c883:
A portfolio that supports affordable home cooling and routine hot-day outreach deserves comparison with an emergency-center-only strategy.
Qualification: Candidate strategy inferred from the timing of estimated mortality; these sources do not establish its marginal cost-effectiveness. The emergency-center-only comparator is hypothetical, not a description of NYC policy. Self-reported barriers alone cannot identify causal effects.
Primary sources: https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/about/press/pr2026/nyc-health-department-releases-report-on-heat-related-deaths.page | https://a816-dohbesp.nyc.gov/IndicatorPublic/data-features/heat-report/
